subject: Media Literacy
title: Media Consolidation
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Media Consolidation.

hook.text: Six companies control 90% of American media. In 1983, fifty companies shared that space. The trend is accelerating.

buildup.text: Media consolidation is the concentration of media ownership in fewer and fewer corporate hands.

discovery.text: Fewer owners means fewer editorial perspectives, less local coverage, and more uniform national narratives.

twist.text: Consolidated media companies prioritize profitable content over public interest journalism that doesn't generate revenue.

climax.text: When a few corporations control most media, democracy loses the diversity of voices it needs to function.

punchline.text: Fewer owners, fewer voices. Diversity of media is diversity of thought.

quiz.question: What is a consequence of media consolidation?
options: Fewer editorial perspectives and less local coverage
